planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in very well-drained, lean, gritty soil in full sun; like other lemon thyme cultivars it is prone to crown rot in humid, poorly drained conditions and appreciates a raised bed or container in the Gulf South.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, gritty soil in full sun; Bertram Anderson is a golden-leaved lemon thyme cultivar prized as much for its bright chartreuse-yellow foliage, which deepens toward green in summer heat, as for its citrus-scented culinary use, making it a useful low, spreading edger that lights up a sunny herb bed or path edge. The lemon-thyme flavor and fragrance are shared with green-leaved lemon thyme and work well in the same fish, poultry, and tea preparations. Shear lightly after flowering to keep the low mat tidy and encourage fresh, brightly colored new growth, and ensure sharp drainage year-round, since wet feet in humid climates are the most common cause of failure.
